verdict.rationale: The quickstart describes an in-session `/upload` slash command and presents the Web UI as an alternative way to chat. Together these indicate a terminal chat session is the default experience when running a llamafile. A community user also praises the 'CLI interface' UX, and the `--cli` flag offers a prompt-answering CLI mode, though that mode reads as one-shot rather than interactive. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement and walkthrough of the interactive terminal chat mode (launch command, multi-turn behavior, available commands), and independent hands-on confirmation of multi-turn terminal chat specifically.

support.subject: As a developer, I can start an interactive chat session with a model directly from the terminal

citations.quote: you can also upload an image by using the `/upload` command and specifying the path to the image
you can also chat with it using [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp)'s Web UI
If you add the `--cli` argument to a llamafile, you will run a CLI version of the model that answers to whatever you provide as a prompt
The llamafile UX (CLI interface and web server with chat) is great
